anchor.quote: That fondness for science, by which God has distinguished the Imam al-Mamun, the Commander of the Faithful... has encouraged me to compose a short work on calculating by al-jabr and al-muqabala, confining it to what is easiest and most useful in arithmetic.

body: Al-Khwarizmi's dedication to the Abbasid caliph al-Mamun. The word 'al-jabr' (completion/restoration) gives us 'algebra'; the Latinization of the author's name gives us 'algorithm'. A direct line from Abbasid Baghdad's House of Wisdom into the European mathematical vocabulary.

anchor.quote: Medicine is the science by which we learn the various states of the human body, when in health and when not in health, whereby health is conserved and whereby it is restored after being lost.
anchor.locator: Book I, on the definition of medicine

body: Avicenna's definition opens the Canon, the systematizing medical encyclopaedia that served as the standard teaching text in both Islamic and (in Latin translation) European medical schools into the 17th century.

anchor.quote: Charles the King, our great Emperor, has been seven full years in Spain: he has conquered the high land down to the sea.

body: The opening of the Old French epic that mythologized Charlemagne's 778 Pyrenean campaign. As history it is unreliable; as a window onto 11th–12th-century crusading ideology and Frankish identity it is invaluable.

anchor.quote: Justice is the constant and perpetual will to render to each his due. The precepts of the law are these: to live honourably, to injure no one, to give each his own.

body: Justinian's restatement of the maxims of Roman law. Rediscovered at Bologna in the 11th–12th centuries, the Corpus became the seed of the medieval ius commune and the European civil-law tradition.

anchor.quote: There was no single hide nor a yard of land, nor indeed one ox nor one cow nor one pig which was left out, and not put down in his record.
anchor.locator: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, entry for 1085 (describing the survey)

body: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle's description of the exhaustiveness of William I's 1086 survey — the most complete record of land, livestock, and obligation in any medieval European kingdom, and the fiscal backbone of Norman royal administration.

anchor.quote: The object of this treatise is to enlighten a religious man who has been trained to believe in the truth of our holy Law, who conscientiously fulfils his moral and religious duties, and at the same time has been successful in his philosophical studies.

body: Maimonides' project of reconciling Aristotelian philosophy with Jewish scripture, written in Judaeo-Arabic in Ayyubid Cairo. It shaped not only Jewish thought but, through Latin translation, the scholasticism of Aquinas.

anchor.quote: No free man shall be seized or imprisoned, or stripped of his rights or possessions, or outlawed or exiled, or deprived of his standing in any other way, nor will we proceed with force against him, or send others to do so, except by the lawful judgement of his equals or by the law of the land.

body: The foundational due-process guarantee — judgement by peers and the law of the land — that binds the English crown to legal limits. Routinely cited as the lineage of habeas corpus and trial by jury.

anchor.quote: To no one will we sell, to no one deny or delay right or justice.

body: The promise against the sale and delay of justice — the principle behind a right to a fair and timely trial.

anchor.quote: In the city of Kemenfu the Great Khan has built a huge palace of marble and other ornamental stones. Round this palace a wall is built, enclosing a compass of sixteen miles, and inside the park there are fountains and rivers and brooks, and beautiful meadows.

body: Polo's account of Kublai Khan's summer capital at Shangdu — a key European source for the wealth and administration of the Yuan court, however filtered through Rustichello's romance framing.

anchor.quote: Royal authority and large-scale dynastic power are attained only through a group and group feeling (asabiyyah). This is because aggressive and defensive strength is obtained only through group feeling which means affection and willingness to fight and die for each other.

body: Ibn Khaldun's theory of asabiyyah (social cohesion) as the engine of the rise and decline of dynasties — a founding text of historiography and the philosophy of history, written from the vantage of the post-Almohad Maghreb.

anchor.quote: We are about to found a school for the Lord's service. In drawing up its regulations, we hope to set down nothing harsh, nothing burdensome.

body: The founding charter of Western cenobitic monasticism. The 'school for the Lord's service' framing shaped the rhythm of labour, prayer, and stability (the vow not to wander) across Latin Christendom for a thousand years.

anchor.quote: Because the doctor of Catholic truth ought not only to teach the proficient, but also to instruct beginners... we purpose in this book to treat of whatever belongs to the Christian religion, in such a way as may tend to the instruction of beginners.

body: Aquinas's stated pedagogical aim frames the Summa's quaestio method — objections, sed contra, response, replies — the high-scholastic engine of the medieval universities.
